annotation.title_clean: Why police robots will not become human-like: social interaction, machine ethics, and limits of AI
annotation.title_en: Why police robots will not become human-like: social interaction, machine ethics, and limits of AI
annotation.summary_en: Philosophical open-forum paper arguing that human-like police robots capable of open-ended social interaction, discretionary norm application and accountable coercive authority cannot be built, due to inherent limits of AI. Robots may still assist in narrow tasks under human oversight; responsibility gaps and legitimacy concerns persist.
key_provisions_or_claims: Strong infeasibility thesis: human-like police robots for open-ended social policing cannot be built.
Teleoperated, bomb-disposal and constrained human-in-the-loop robots are not the target and may be justified.
Policing legitimacy depends on procedural justice, discretion and accountability that machines cannot supply.
Robotic errors (hallucinations) are opaque, systematic and weaken responsibility attribution.
Safety gains are conditional on robust human oversight and conservative operational constraints.
